Section B
Answer all the questions.
You may use the case study, your own enterprise experience and your knowledge of enterprise
where appropriate to answer the following questions.

text: Paul ignored Harriet’s advice to produce a business plan.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Harriet thought that customers might complain when they realise where the materials for their
new furniture had come from.
Discuss why it is important for the long-term success of Paul’s enterprise idea that he deals
with customer complaints.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Paul researched possible sources of finance, including government grants.
Evaluate whether a government grant would be the most suitable source of finance for Paul’s
enterprise idea. You should consider two other sources of finance in your answer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Paul considered the views and interests of a number of people, known as stakeholders, who
might be affected by his enterprise idea.
Discuss the importance of considering the views and interests of different stakeholders to the
start-up and success of your enterprise project.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Paul used oral and written communication within his enterprise.
Evaluate whether oral or written communication was, or could have been, most effective
within your enterprise project when communicating with two of the following:
• financial institutions
• suppliers
• customers
• another stakeholder.
